sentences.text: This is the first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 filed on behalf of the applicant for grant of bail.

The applicant is in custody since 09.12.2022 in connection with Crime No.1874/2022 registered at Police Station Lasudiya, District Indore (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under sections 366, 376, 376(2)(n), 377 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code of 1860.
As per prosecution story, prosecutrix is major and married lady.
Present applicant Rahul Sharma developed friendship with her and after sometime he told that he wants to marry with her.
In the month of February, 2022, on the pretext of marriage, present applicant established physical relationship with her and assured her that after getting divorce from his wife he will marry her.

sentences.text: sometime husband of the prosecutrix expelled the prosecutrix from his house.
On 03.10.2022 prosecutrix went to the present applicant's house, there present applicant denied to live with her.
Accordingly, offence has been registered against the applicant.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is an innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this offence.
He is in custody since 09.12.2022.
Prosecutrix is a major and married lady.
She knows that present applicant was also married person.
Therefore, no offence under Section 376 of IPC is made out in the instant case.
Investigation is over and charge-sheet has been filed.
Applicant is permanent resident of Indore district.
Final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time.
Hence, he prays that applicant be enlarged on bail.

Per contra, learned counsel for the objector opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection by submitting that on the pretext of marriage present applicant exploited her and established physical relationship with her, due to which she got divorce from her husband, later on present applicant denied to live with her.
Therefore, he does not deserve for bail.
Learned counsel for the respondent / State also opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection.
Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case diary.

Learned counsel for the applicant placed reliance upon the judgment of the Apex Curt in the case of Prashant Bharti Vs. NCT of Delhi AIR 2013 Supreme Court 2753 in which it has been held that under Penal Code (45 of 1860), S.376- Rape- Complainant alleging that her consent was obtained under promise of marriage- Complainant found to be already married at relevant time- Obtaining consent of married woman for sex on assurance of marriage is incomprehensible - allegation of complainant stands falsified.

sentences.text:
After considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature and gravity of offence,
arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant and also taking note of the fact that prosecutrix is major and married lady, she got divorce from her husband vide judgment dated 16.12.2022 passed by the II Additional Judge Family Court, Indore in H.M.A. Case No.2253/2022

entities.text: II Additional Judge Family Court, Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
,
she remained in the company of present applicant for more than one year, so many photographs and whatsapp chatting have been filed to prove the love affairs between present applicant and prosecutrix, investigation is over and charge- sheet has been filed, therefore, no further custodial interrogation of the present applicant is required and final conclusion of the trial will take sufficient long time.
In view of the above, without commenting on the merits of the case, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
Therefore, the application is allowed.

It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/-
(Rupees Seventy Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) Cr.P.C.
